interpretation: Robot: agilex_piper_sim, one 6-joint arm, parallel-jaw gripper (stroke 70 mm, max width 66 mm, closed_empty 0.97, held_below 0.93, tip_reach 2 cm), scene cameras 'left'/'right' and a 'wrist' camera. Scene: a white 3D printer (perceived as obj1 frame, obj3 column, obj4 top gantry arm, obj2 grey slot behind the bed) with a removable dark build plate obj5 (19x19x1.3 cm, top z~0.085, x[-0.024,0.167] y[-0.477,-0.287]). The 'finished print' is obj6+obj7: an orange hexagonal part (flat-to-flat 43.8 mm, corner-to-corner ~50 mm, 13.5 mm tall, top z~0.098) with a raised blue circular boss (diameter ~2 cm, top z~0.101) in the centre, initially at about (0.0775,-0.402). The 'black shelf' is obj8, a black box in front of the printer (top z~0.065, x[0.174,0.301] y[-0.502,-0.264]), 2 cm lower than the plate. Goal: print resting on top of the black shelf; build plate still on the printer, not dragged or lifted. Ambiguity: the instruction does not specify the print's orientation on the shelf.
plan: Initial plan: tilted top-down grasp of the hex across two flats (pure top-down was unreachable because joint5 is limited to +-70 deg; high-elbow solutions collide with the printer's gantry), lift straight up so the plate stays, carry to the shelf, place, release. The approach chosen was azimuth -123..-124.5 deg, 30 deg from vertical, closing across the 145.5 deg flat normal, which was collision-free. Two grasp attempts failed: the tapered fingertips only reached the top few mm of the 13.5 mm wall, and on closing the gripper rode up over the hex and pinched the blue boss (readings 0.774 and 0.886). Each release kicked the print (15 mm, then ~40 mm, to ~1.6 cm from the plate edge). Near-vertical and side grasps were either blocked by the gantry or would put the finger bodies into the plate. So I switched to a non-prehensile plan: straddle the print with the open gripper (fingers along x, approach az -85 deg, 20 deg below horizontal), push it in +x with the rear finger's inner face to the plate's front edge, and let it drop 2 cm onto the shelf. The drop left it tilted 45 deg and then standing on edge, so I added a forward push and a low slide (rear finger below the print's centre of mass) to move it clear of the plate edge before it fell flat.

steps.what: Read embodiment, instruction, objects; annotated left/right images; heightmap and closeup of the print
steps.why: Identify the print, plate, shelf and their heights
steps.result: Print = orange hex obj6 + blue boss obj7 on plate obj5; shelf = obj8 (top 0.065). Step 0.

steps.what: IK scans: top-down, tilted along radial, then other azimuths with collision checks
steps.result: Top-down unreachable; radial/az -63 approaches put link3 into the printer gantry (obj4/obj1); az -123 at 30-60 deg from horizontal was arm-collision-free.

steps.what: Estimated the hex orientation from the cloud (min sum of widths over 3 flat normals), confirmed by projecting the corners on the wrist image and refining with the dense wrist cloud
steps.result: Flat normals 26.5/86.5/146.5 deg, flat-to-flat 43.8 mm; centre refined to (0.0728,-0.4012).

steps.what: Moved to the pre-grasp via FK of a joint-space interpolation (a straight Cartesian line was unreachable), then descended along the approach axis and lowered 2.5 mm with tracking-error feed-forward
steps.why: Reach the grasp pose safely and centred
steps.result: TCP (0.0722,-0.400,0.1098), 1.1 mm off-centre; print between the open fingers (images/018, 021). Step 136.

Reading 0.774 (gap 15.8 mm, far below the 43.8 mm hex): the fingers rode up 1.9 mm, closed over the hex top and pinched the blue boss (images/027, 028). Scene-depth finger points bottomed out at z~0.100.
Opening kicked the print ~15 mm and left a finger on it, tilted 6 deg. After lifting it settled flat at (0.0812,-0.4107). Perception merged it into the plate, so I defined agent object 'print'.

steps.what: Re-grasp approach commanded to TCP z 0.100 (az -124.5, closing 145.5)
steps.why: Get the fingertips lower on the wall
steps.result: TCP stopped at z 0.1085 with a 0.05 rad joint5 error (resting on something); after raising 0.6 mm and closing (attempt 2): reading 0.886 (gap 8 mm), the TCP rose 6.3 mm and the fingers again ended on top of the hex at the boss (images/040). Step 303.
Print kicked ~40 mm to (0.1145,-0.4356), rotated 16 deg, 1.6 cm from the plate edge (images/041).

steps.what: Measured the real finger length by projecting TCP+0..4 cm marks along the finger lines onto a zoomed scene image
steps.why: Earlier inferences about the fingertips were inconsistent
steps.result: Tapered fingers reach ~2-2.5 cm past the TCP (images/043). From above, only the tapered tip section can touch a 13.5 mm wall, which explains the ride-up; near-vertical grasps collide with the gantry. Decided to push instead.

steps.what: Moved to a straddle pose (lift, re-orient at height via joint interpolation, descend): open gripper, closing axis ~x, approach az -85 deg, 20 deg below horizontal, TCP (0.12,-0.4225,~0.105-0.11)
steps.why: Cage the print between the fingers so the rear finger's inner face can push its back flat in +x; this TCP range (x>=0.105) keeps the elbow clear of the printer
steps.result: Print between the fingers, plate untouched (images/045). Step 446.

steps.what: Push stage 1: TCP x 0.12 -> 0.17 at constant height
steps.why: Slide the print to the plate's front edge
steps.result: Print slid flat to the plate edge (images/047). Step 510.

steps.what: Push stage 2: TCP x 0.17 -> 0.205 (first preview refused by my own check: finger spheres vs obj1, which had absorbed the plate; re-checked allowing only gripper-sphere contacts)
steps.why: Push the print past the edge onto the shelf
steps.result: Print dropped but came to rest tilted ~45 deg, front edge on the shelf, rear propped on the plate edge or the rear finger (images/051). Step 552.

steps.why: Tip or slide it clear of the plate edge
steps.result: Print stood on edge on the shelf at x~0.20, leaning back on the rear finger (images/053). Step 594.

steps.what: Lowered the gripper (rear finger ~1 cm above the shelf, below the print's centre of mass) and slid forward to TCP x 0.275
steps.why: Slide rather than tip, so it lands clear of the plate edge
steps.result: Print fell flat onto the shelf, upside down (boss down), tilt 2.7 deg (images/055). Step 658.

steps.what: Lifted the gripper straight up 8 cm and verified with both scene cameras and the cloud
steps.why: Retract without disturbing; check every part of the instruction
steps.result: Print (obj19) x[0.194,0.232] y[-0.444,-0.403], top z 0.081, entirely inside the shelf top x[0.174,0.301] y[-0.502,-0.264]. Plate-top extent x[-0.018,0.162] y[-0.474,-0.294] matches its start, so it is still on the printer (images/056, 057, 058). Finished at step 692 of 2700.

diagnosis: I believe the stated goal holds: the print is off the plate, resting flat and entirely on the black shelf, and the plate is unmoved on the printer (checked in both scene cameras and the point cloud). Remaining risk: the print is upside down (boss down, ~2.7 deg tilt from resting on its boss). An evaluator expecting it upright, or expecting a pick-and-place rather than pushing and dropping it over the 2 cm step, could score it lower. Why the grasp failed: the sim PiPER's fingers are tapered and reach ~2-2.5 cm past the TCP. From a 30 deg tilted top approach (the only collision-free one; steeper ones put link3 into the gantry), only the tapered lower finger section could touch the 13.5 mm wall. Closing pushed the gripper up over the hex (the arm is compliant in z), so it pinched the 3 mm boss instead. Each release kicked the print 1.5-4 cm, nearly to the plate edge. Done differently: measure the finger geometry with a scene-camera zoom before the first close, and skip the top grasp for such a short part. Go straight to the caged push, sliding the print over the plate edge with the pusher low (below its centre of mass) and continuing until its whole footprint is past the edge, so it lands flat and upright. Or test a boss pinch with a short lift before releasing.
lessons: Before grasping a short object, measure the real finger shape and reach: zoom a scene camera on the open gripper with TCP+k*approach marks. Here the tapered fingers reached ~2-2.5 cm past the TCP, and only the tip section could touch a 13.5 mm wall from above.

If a close reads far narrower than the object (0.77-0.89 for a 44 mm part) and the TCP rises during the close, the fingers rode over the object. Do not release without a plan: each release kicked the print 1.5-4 cm.

The PiPER sim's position control is compliant, with steady-state errors of 2-6 mm (joint5 0.03-0.05 rad). A TCP that stays several mm above the commanded height, with a joint error that does not shrink during hold(), means contact. Feed forward the observed xy error when centring.
When a straight Cartesian move is unreachable, use FK waypoints from a joint-space interpolation. Lift first and re-orient at height, so the swing does not pass low over objects.

In this cell the printer gantry (top arm and column) blocks high-elbow solutions. Arm-collision-free approaches for parts on the plate were about az -85 to -95 deg (closing along x, low tilt) and az -124 to -141 deg (30 deg from vertical).

A caged push (open gripper straddling the part, rear finger pushing a flat) moves a short part reliably. To get it over a step without tilting, push low (below its centre of mass) and keep going until its whole footprint is past the edge.

Perception merges or drops a part near the gripper, and an agent object left behind becomes a phantom. Re-measure the part from orange/blue cloud points after every motion, and forget stale agent objects.
